speaker: any
text: This is getting intense. Members are recruiting in their sleep; Gary recruited a man while napping. People are skipping work, meals and in one case their own wedding for {belief}. Something has to give.

choices.label: Cool things down.
choices.reaction: You cancel two {meetings} and announce a “gentle week”. It is the most controversial thing you have ever done.

choices.label: Channel it into one great {meeting}.
choices.reaction: The great {meeting} runs for nineteen hours. Everyone goes home exhausted and, briefly, normal.

speaker: any
text: Last {day}, eleven people came. Nine were there for the warmth. One was lost. The mood is flat, {title}. People are drifting away.

choices.label: Throw a party.
choices.reaction: The party has a theme, a playlist and, crucially, a reason to come back.

choices.label: Remind them why we started.
choices.reaction: You tell the story of Gary’s garage. Half the room is moved. The other half was not there and feels left out.

speaker: any
text: Nobody has disagreed with anything in months. Every vote is unanimous. Dez has stopped having ideas, which has never happened. It’s unsettling, {title}.

choices.label: Invite disagreement.
choices.reaction: The first disagreement in months is about chairs. Everyone is relieved.

choices.label: Hold an open forum.
choices.reaction: The forum produces forty-one complaints, three ideas and one excellent cake.

speaker: any
text: Three factions have formed around the snack table. Nobody will sit with anybody. Someone has started a rival newsletter, and it is better than ours.

choices.label: Emergency all-member {meeting}.
choices.reaction: The emergency {meeting} ends with a group handshake. It takes eleven minutes, but it is a handshake.

choices.label: Let each faction run its own night.
choices.reaction: Three {meeting} nights, three snack tables, one uneasy peace.

text: The council has questions. So do two newspapers, a radio station and a man who keeps filming {hq} from a hedge.

choices.label: Hold a press conference.
choices.reaction: You answer every question. The man in the hedge asks the last one. He seems satisfied.

choices.label: Go quiet for a month.
choices.reaction: {Movement} goes quiet. The hedge man waits. Then the hedge man leaves.

speaker: any
text: Nobody knows we exist. I asked someone at the bus stop about {movement}. He thought I was selling insurance.

choices.label: A big public stunt.
choices.reaction: The stunt involves {belief}, a brass band and the fountain. Nobody forgets it.

choices.label: Door to door, the old way.
choices.reaction: Members knock on six thousand doors. Two thousand open. Forty people join. It is a start.

speaker: any
text: We have more money than we know what to do with. People are proposing a fountain. Rolf, or someone very like him, wants a yacht.

choices.label: Give it to the community.
choices.reaction: The new benches in {hometown} each carry a small plaque. Some are already being sat on with conviction.

choices.label: Invest it in organisers.
choices.reaction: Three paid organisers are hired. Volunteers wonder why they are not paid. The question will not go away.

speaker: any
text: We are out of money. The hall wants rent, the urn needs descaling, and someone has been paying for the biscuits personally. It is Gary.

choices.label: Pass the hat.
choices.hint: Members chip in · Some resent it
choices.reaction: The hat comes back heavier than expected. Several members put in IOUs. One puts in a pebble.

choices.label: Sell the megaphone.
choices.reaction: The megaphone fetches a surprising sum. Dez attends the sale in a black armband.
